subject: hoverPickup
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: militarized pickup converted to hover thrusters.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module for a hover pickup truck, roughly 4.8m long, 2m wide, 1.9m high, facing +Z, with four hover thrusters replacing wheels instead of a full creature skeleton.

I'm working out the hovering mechanics—thruster pods acting as landing skids keep the lowest points near y=0—and sketching the construction approach using boxes, frustums, and extrusions for the silhouette, pairing a glow kit with custom paint for decals like neon stripes, headlights, stenciled stars, hazard stripes, and a HUD screen. I'm laying out the body coordinates along the z-axis: chassis, sloped hood, cab, and bed walls, each with specific height and depth ranges.

Now I'm plotting the extruded profile outline point by point—rear and front bottoms, hood slope, windshield, roof, rear cab—making sure the shape stays non-self-intersecting as a clean CCW polygon.

Still outlining body points, then I'm figuring out the windshield as a thin tilted glass slab positioned at the slope midpoint, computing its rotation and offset along the surface normal.

Now I'm sketching side windows as thin extruded polygons along the cab's side profile, placing them just outside the body surface at x=±0.85 with a small thickness so they sit flush against the cab walls.

Now I'm adding military armor details: hood and roof plates, a light bar, armored bed panels, and a roof-mounted turret gun with ring mount, barrel, and body. I'm filling the bed with cargo like a rocket pod and crates plus an antenna, then placing four thruster nacelles at the rear corners with ducted shrouds, glow rings, and fan blade textures facing downward toward the ground plane.

Adding more vehicle details...

Now I'm planning headlight glow planes flanking the grill, then working out door decal panels on the sides with stenciled numbers and star markings, positioning them to read upright on the body's flat side faces.

I'm planning the body paint as a matte gunmetal with darker/lighter patches for camo, plus magenta and cyan accent neon colors. I'm adding neon tube stripes along the sides and a two-tone cyan/magenta glowing roof light bar for the cyberpunk look.

Now I'm figuring out the rear details: a lathed antenna dish, bed ribs, and cargo options. I'm deciding to place a gun turret mounted in the bed rear with a lathed base and twin barrels, plus small cargo crates and side-mounted missile pods along the bed walls instead of cluttering the roof.

Building bed wall geometry with slanted armor panels and glowing trim strips, then figuring out fender arms connecting the body to the thruster pods so the pod radius tucks neatly against the body width.

Adding glow ring tori around the shroud at varying heights, using cyan with magenta underglow accents, plus a faint downward-facing glow disc at the bottom of the pod.

I'm reworking the shroud geometry to open at the bottom, lowering the lathe outline and repositioning the glow disc so it's visible from below at a reasonable height, keeping total model height around 2.3 units including the antenna. Now I'm planning out the texture atlas list, starting with fan blades, door stencils, and grille/headlight details.

For the rest of the vehicle, I'm adding hazard markings, a hud window texture, and a license plate, bringing texture count to roughly seven. I'm also deciding to skip interior dashboard detail but add cab seat boxes behind tinted, gradient-painted windshield glass, plus side mirrors, door handles, and rear hover vents with glowing tips, along with a central horizontal nozzle pod at the tail.

Now I'm placing the rear nozzle with its glow disc, positioning tail light bars on either side of it, and sizing the rear wall box to properly cover the tail structure. I'm also sketching helper functions for boxes, glow effects, and planes to streamline building out these remaining parts.

I'm setting up mirrored geometry across both sides, then defining the paint schemes: a countershaded body paint with patchy coloring, a mottled plate texture, and a dark mottled iron finish for armored sections.

Now I'm planning the roof light bar split into magenta/cyan glowing halves, then designing the turret-mounted gun assembly with a lathed base, boxy housing, twin barrels, and checking that barrel height clears the cab roof so it doesn't intersect geometry.

Placing the light bar and gun housing on the roof, then moving to the truck bed where I'll add rocket pods and crates. I'm figuring out how to orient a rocket pod box with a textured top showing launch tube holes, considering whether to tilt it or keep it upright.

I also plan an antenna with a glowing tip, side skirts with glow strips, and a cyberpunk neon decal reading "ARC·HOVER" on the bed walls. I'm now writing a helper function for placing textured decal planes onto the model.

Designing fan, door, and grill textures...

Now mapping out the remaining texture sets: a glowing head bar, hazard stripes, tail segments, pod-top glowing tubes, and a neon magenta/cyan bed sign with glow outlines. I'm also deciding that painted body parts stay flat without glow, while glass gets a dark emissive tint for a subtle cyan glow effect.

Working through the body construction details: the thickness/extrusion axes for the main shell, placement of hood vents and an armor ridge along the hood centerline, with colors layered dark and magenta/orange accents on top.

Now I'm adjusting the hood's slight backward rise to recalculate vent height, then placing mirrors, door handles, and glowing skirt rods along the sides — checking that the thruster pods don't overlap the body at their current radius.

I'm deciding to skip extra strut boxes, winglets, and bolt rings on the pods since they'd be mostly hidden or unnecessary, and considering the design essentially complete.

Now I'm working on the rear nozzle as a lathed shape positioned at the tail, with a glowing end disc facing backward, making sure it sits within the body's tail opening without colliding with the tail wall or the rear lights.
